category: AI System Design, Production Serving & LLMOps

content.tldr: Systematic LLM evaluation pairs deterministic metrics with automated LLM-as-a-Judge frameworks (RAGAS) across Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, and Context Precision.
content.simple_explanation: Evaluating probabilistic generative text requires moving beyond simple string equality. Production evaluation pipelines apply automated multi-metric testing: deterministic code checks (valid JSON syntax, schema compliance), rule-based toxicity filters, and model-based judges. The RAGAS framework assesses three primary pillars: Faithfulness (is the answer grounded strictly in retrieved context without hallucination?), Answer Relevance (does the answer directly address the query?), and Context Precision (did retrieval avoid noisy irrelevant chunks?).
content.real_world_example: A university grading board: multiple-choice tests are graded automatically by machine; student essays are graded against a detailed standardized rubric by an independent senior evaluator assessing coherence and factual grounding.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: LLM judges exhibit inherent biases, including position bias (favoring whichever passage is presented first), verbosity bias (favoring longer responses), and self-enhancement bias (scoring generations from their own model family higher). Always swap comparison order and calibrate judge models against human annotators.
